message.content:
The sea usually looks **blue**—but it’s more complex than just one shade:

| Factor | Effect on Color |
|--------|----------------|
| **Depth & water clarity** | Deeper or clearer waters appear deeper‑bluer; shallow or murky areas look greener or even brownish because suspended particles scatter sunlight differently. |
| **Sun angle / time of day** | Early morning or late afternoon gives warm hues (golden, pink), while midday sun makes the surface sparkle bright turquoise/azure. |
| **Algae & phytoplankton** | High concentrations give green or teal tones. |
| **Sediment runoff** | Rivers carrying silt can tint coastal seas reddish/brown. |

So while “the sea” often conjures images of deep azure, its actual hue depends on location, weather, season, and what’s floating in the water.
